facts.statement: Albertavenator is a small-bodied troodontid theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Albertavenator (meaning "Alberta hunter") is a genus of small-bodied troodontid theropod dinosaur

facts.statement: The fossils of Albertavenator were found in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: It is known from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta, Canada

facts.statement: Albertavenator is classified in the family Troodontidae within the clade Paraves.
facts.quote: Albertavenator is assigned to the family Troodontidae within the clade Paraves

facts.statement: The environment where Albertavenator lived was much cooler than other nearby formations.
facts.quote: It was much cooler in temperature than other formations nearby

facts.statement: A skull fragment found in 1993 at the Bleriot ferry on the Red Deer River was initially mistaken for a Troodon fossil.
facts.quote: En 1993, se encontró un trozo de cráneo en el ferry Bleriot en el río Red Deer que primero se confundió con un fósil de Troodon

facts.statement: Albertavenator curriei was named and described in 2017 by David C. Evans, Thomas M. Cullen, Derek W. Larson, and Adam Rego.
facts.quote: En 2017, David C. Evans, Thomas M. Cullen, Derek W. Larson y Adam Rego nombraron y describieron la especie tipo Albertavenator curriei

facts.statement: The top surface of the frontal bone is relatively shorter than in all other known troodontids, being less than 30% longer than it is wide.
facts.quote: La superficie superior del hueso frontal es relativamente más corta que en todos los demás troodóntidos conocidos, siendo menos del 30% más larga que ancha

facts.statement: Albertavenator is distinguished from other Canadian materials, and it was proposed to no longer assign it to Troodon because that taxon is based on teeth.
facts.quote: Albertavenator se destaca de otros materiales canadienses. Se propuso ya no asignarlo a Troodon ya que este taxón se basa en dientes

facts.statement: The time range for Albertavenator spans from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
